question.text: Lotus Growth Fund (Category II AIF) owns 15% of Zephyr Logistics, an unlisted company. Zephyr's FY25 EBITDA is INR 40 crore. Peer-set trading EV/EBITDA is 12x. Zephyr's net debt is INR 80 crore. Using the relative valuation approach with no illiquidity discount applied, what is the fair value of Lotus's stake in Zephyr?

explanation.text: The Logic: EV = 12 x INR 40 cr EBITDA = INR 480 cr. Equity Value = EV - Net Debt = 480 - 80 = INR 400 cr. Lotus's 15% stake = 0.15 x 400 = INR 60 crore. The textbook computation under Section 14.7.1 requires deducting debt from EV to reach equity. The Trap: INR 72 cr applies 15% to EV directly (forgets debt). INR 48 cr uses only EBITDA x multiple x stake. INR 54 cr adds back cash incorrectly. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) uses the same EV/EBITDA method but with a listed-peer lens; XIX-C stresses the illiquidity discount and unlisted-comp adjustment typical in PE valuation. Manager's Pro-Tip: At the IC, always show BOTH the EV and the equity bridge in the valuation memo. LPs reviewing the quarterly NAV will push back if the debt adjustment is missing — this is the most common audit finding in AIF valuation reports.
